newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sues Tennessee county, seeks to force tax.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sues Tennessee county, seeks to force tax.

text.p: The federal government has filed suite against Tennessee's Hickman County, accusing the county of fraudulently collecting disaster relief funds for damaged bridges, a county official said Friday.
The lawsuit asks the U.S. District Court in Nashville to order the county to levy a tax on its residents to repay the money, County Executive Stephen Gregory said.

The suit alleges that Hickman County submitted 16 fraudulent claims involving eight bridges, and seeks $1.7 million in repayment. A judgement agaisnt the county could cost each of its 19,086 residents $88.49, Gregory said.
County officials sought federal emergency funds for bridge replacement after flooding in 1991 qualified Hickman County for disaster relief.
The lawsuit alleges that in some cases, bridges were deliberately destroyed in an attempt to obtain federal money to replace them.
It said that state inspectors viewed the bridges immediately after the flooding and determined that although they were damaged they could be repaired.
But when inspectors with the Federal Emergency Management Agency came to examine the bridges, some of the spans had been pushed off their abutments into creeks, the suit alleges.
In another case, a purportedly damaged bridge had not existed before the flood.
"In fact, no bridge had been at that site for many years," the lawsuit said.
Two employees of the county southwest of Nashville are also named in the suit.
